title: Base editing for precision therapeutics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplementary archive (14.96 MB). It contains only mmc1.pdf (4 pages: Figure S1 plus Table S1) and mmc2.pdf (the article PDF itself), plus 8 figure images (.gif/.webp). I extracted the text of mmc1.pdf: Table S1 is a free-text comparison of gene-delivery vehicles (AAV, lentivirus, VLP, extracellular vesicles, etc.) whose 'editing efficiency' cells are prose like '~40% in vivo (mouse rd10 rescue)' or 'N/A'. No CSV, TSV, XLSX or any machine-readable table exists. Searched the 439,052-character full text and Europe PMC's text-mined accessions: the only identifiers are 17 ClinicalTrials.gov trial numbers (e.g. NCT05442346) and funder DOIs. No GEO, SRA, BioProject, dbGaP or Zenodo/Dryad record is linked.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The article's own framing as a narrative review of base-editing therapeutics, and the clinical efficacy figures it quotes (e.g. 74.4% PCSK9 and 52.3% LDL-C reduction for YOLT-101 at 24 weeks), which are secondary citations to other papers rather than data deposited here. The 'Supplemental information' footnote lists only 'Document S1. Figure S1 and Table S1' and 'Document S2. Article plus supplemental information'.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified in the files. The paper is a narrative review and deposits no dataset. The supplement downloads fine but contains only two PDFs and figure images; there is no data repository accession anywhere in the text or in Europe PMC's cross-reference and text-mining records.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified. No column of any kind exists. The closest thing to an outcome is the 'Editing Efficiency Range' cell of Table S1, which is free prose ('~63% in vivo (mouse liver)', '15-40% in vitro', 'N/A'), so any label would have to be hand-constructed from sentences.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL, verified. No guide RNA sequences, target sequences, protein sequences or molecular structures appear in the supplement. The only machine-readable identifiers are 17 clinical trial registration numbers, which would each need a separate lookup.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL, verified. The efficiency values in Table S1 are percentages mixed across cell types, species, assays and in vitro versus in vivo settings, with no consistent denominator and no stated measurement protocol.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified. Table S1 spans 4 PDF pages with on the order of 20-30 delivery-vehicle rows, far under the ~400-row floor for classification. I did not count exactly because the table is not machine-readable.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small, but only because there is nothing in it. Passing A6 is meaningless here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not applicable: the paper states no row counts because it reports no dataset. Scored as a failure rather than a pass so it is not mistaken for a verified match.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL, verified. Every efficiency number in Table S1 is a figure quoted from a cited primary paper, not a measurement made here. Provenance would have to be chased through ~260 references, with different editors, cell lines and readouts behind each.

existing_models.name: BE-Hive (Arbab et al., Cell 2020) - gradient-boosted trees plus a deep autoregressive model predicting base-editing efficiency and the exact genotype produced
existing_models.score_and_split: Pearson correlation about 0.9 for genotype outcome and about 0.7 for efficiency; R = 0.69-0.80 for adenine base editors and 0.53-0.74 for cytosine base editors on held-out target sequences in mouse embryonic stem cells.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer across cell types and across base-editor variants not seen in training.

existing_models.name: BE-DICT (Marquart et al., Nature Communications 2021) - attention-based (transformer-style) deep network for base-editing outcomes
existing_models.score_and_split: Pearson r = 0.78 for ABEmax, 0.68 for CBE4max, 0.57 for ABE8e and 0.64 for Target-AID; trained on a library of 28,294 integrated target sequences.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Accuracy drops for newer, more processive editors such as ABE8e.

existing_models.name: DeepBE (Kim et al., Nature Biotechnology 2023) - deep learning predicting efficiency and outcomes for 63 base-editor/Cas9-variant combinations
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained and evaluated on thousands of target sequences across 7 base editors and 9 Cas9 variants; exact held-out numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Endogenous chromatin context beyond the DNA sequence itself.

existing_models.name: Multi-dataset deep models (Nature Communications 2025) and LLM-EmBEditor (2025) - models trained jointly across several base-editing libraries, the latter using protein/DNA language-model embeddings
existing_models.score_and_split: LLM-EmBEditor reports Pearson R = 0.717 and Spearman rho = 0.797 on a combined adenine-base-editor dataset; the Nature Communications model used roughly 20,000 guide RNAs.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer between editor chemistries (adenine versus cytosine) and between cell contexts.

backbone.name: None applicable - no data of any modality to embed.

integration.partner_dataset: None. The only joinable identifiers are 17 ClinicalTrials.gov trial numbers, which link to trial registry records, not to per-example measurements.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: there is no per-row entity in this paper to join anything to.

controls.positive_control: None possible - no measurements to recover a known signal from.
controls.external_validation: Not applicable here. The real base-editing screen data lives in the primary papers (BE-Hive, BE-DICT, DeepBE and the 2025 SURRO-seq libraries), not in this review.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible from this paper: it is a narrative review whose only supplementary table is a prose comparison of delivery vehicles, so nothing here can train or test a model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use guide RNA and target DNA sequence to predict how efficiently a base editor rewrites a single DNA letter.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model a short DNA target window plus the matching guide RNA and the identity of the base editor used. This paper supplies zero such examples; the published screens it cites hold roughly 11,000-28,000 guides each.
plain_idea.predict: Editing efficiency, meaning the fraction of sequencing reads in which the intended base change occurred, measured by deep sequencing of a library of integrated target sites. This paper reports no such measurements of its own.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gene-therapy groups picking a guide RNA for a disease-causing variant would use it to avoid wet-lab screening, but that need is already served by several open models, and this review contributes no new data toward it.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes no measurements at all, while BE-DICT was trained on 28,294 target sequences and 2025 models on roughly 11,000-20,000 guide RNAs each.

confidence_score.why: There are no replicate measurements, indeed no measurements, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be estimated from anything here.

models_beatable.why: BE-Hive (2020) and BE-DICT (2021) are open and were evaluated on held-out target sequences, and newer 2023-2025 models (DeepBE, LLM-EmBEditor, multi-dataset networks) already push the same task further.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Every condition fails: there is no dataset here to add to a baseline, no join key to per-example data, and no evaluation split.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The task it points at - predicting base-editing efficiency and outcome from guide RNA and target sequence - is real and well posed, but the training data for it sits in the primary screening papers this review cites (BE-Hive, BE-DICT, DeepBE, the 2025 SURRO-seq libraries of ~11,500 guides per editor). If the base-editing area is of interest, evaluate one of those primary datasets directly rather than this review.

effort.compute_note: Only the 15 MB supplementary archive was handled; no modelling workload exists to estimate because there is no dataset.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the supplement and list the file types. Two PDFs and eight images, no tabular file, kills it in under a minute - which is exactly what happened.

verdict_reason: This is a narrative review of base-editing therapeutics, not a data paper. I opened the entire supplementary archive: it holds only a 4-page PDF (one figure plus a free-text table comparing delivery vehicles), the article PDF, and figure images. Part A fails at A1 (no dataset deposited and no repository accession anywhere in the text or in Europe PMC's cross-references), and equally at A2, A3, A4, A5 and A8. Separately, the prediction task the review gestures at is already served by several open, honestly evaluated models (BE-Hive, BE-DICT, DeepBE, plus 2025 multi-dataset and language-model approaches), so even a hypothetical dataset here would enter a crowded field. If base editing is of interest, go to the primary screening papers for their libraries of 11,000-28,000 measured guide RNAs.
